title: Stop-hook (drift-and-ratchet/delegation-canon) blocks normal /loop turn endings, including ones that already called ScheduleWakeup
details:
**What happened:** A user-configured Stop hook (stop-validation.mjs, implementing ~/.claude/canon/delegation-and-stall-discipline.md) fired 14 times in one session, blocking turn endings whenever text matched "stop-language" patterns (e.g. "your call", "which do you want") without a same-turn mcp__ollama-*/WebFetch dispatch. It fired even on a turn whose final action was ScheduleWakeup (a real, substantive continuation mechanism for a /loop-driven session), and re-fired on an already-classified, already-validator-confirmed question with no new information to gain from re-dispatching.
**What the user said:** User didn't comment on the hook directly; observed by the model across the session while working through it repeatedly per the hook's own required-resolution steps (verify substrate, dispatch a validator on the framing, note classification).
**Repro:** Run a /loop-mode session doing real interactive work (not an autonomous conductor mission) with this hook installed; end a turn with a status line mentioning a still-open question for the user, or with ScheduleWakeup as the final action — the hook pattern-matches on phrases like "your call"/"which do you want" and demands a fresh mcp__ollama-*/WebFetch dispatch every time, even for the identical already-answered question, and even when the turn already took a real action.
**Evidence:** Session hook name stop-validation.mjs; canon files ~/.claude/practice/extended/drift-and-ratchet.md and ~/.claude/canon/delegation-and-stall-discipline.md; 14 qualifying fires in one session.
**Cause:** The canon appears designed for autonomous muezzin/conductor mission loops (where "stop language" reaching for the operator mid-unsupervised-run is a real failure mode) but is applied unconditionally to an interactive, human-present Claude Code session and to /loop's own designed ScheduleWakeup-based turn-ending pattern, producing repeated false positives.
